source_identity.identity_method: Exact C27 ACTIVE_WAVE row plus explicit derived_results.id in the sealed source artifact; no label, prefix, semantic or fuzzy join.

candidate_claim: In a specified two-state five-generation Feynman-Kac synthetic model, pilot-estimated generation-wise variance coefficients imply the fixed-budget square-root particle schedule [111,64,46,52,47]. In an independent 30,000-run worker validation using ordered stratified priority resampling at total descendant budget 320, variance was 6.2845445599 versus 7.3185774131 for uniform [64,64,64,64,64], a 14.1289% reduction; reversing the allocation produced variance 9.2858385520, 26.8804% above uniform.

public_primary_support.source: Douc, Cappe, Moulines, Comparison of Resampling Schemes for Particle Filtering, arXiv:cs/0507025
public_primary_support.assessment: Primary theory supports variance improvement of stratified over multinomial in its analyzed setting and gives a counterexample to blanket systematic-resampling variance dominance. It does not prove the worker's five-generation numeric ratios.

public_primary_support.source: Li, Wang, Deng, Liu, Stratification and Optimal Resampling for Sequential Monte Carlo, arXiv:2004.01975 / Biometrika 109(1)
public_primary_support.assessment: Primary theory supports ordered stratification and, in one dimension, its variance-optimal connection to optimal-transport resampling. It does not establish the worker-specific Feynman-Kac gains.

public_primary_support.source: Lee, Whiteley, Variance estimation in the particle filter, arXiv:1509.00394 / Biometrika 105(3)
public_primary_support.assessment: Primary theory supports decomposition/estimation of time-step asymptotic variance contributions from particle genealogy and approximation of asymptotically optimal variable particle-number allocation. This supports the square-root-allocation mechanism class, not the exact finite-model pilot coefficients.

deterministic_reconstruction.method: Independent auditor calculation from the persisted model specification; no worker simulation code used.

auditor_independent_reimplementation.classification: Independent auditor reconstruction from the persisted prose/model contract, not an external third-party replication and not an exact replay of the worker's RNG stream.
auditor_independent_reimplementation.algorithm: Start from 32 particles in each state with exact weights 0.8/32 and 0.2/32; at every generation compute q_i=0.35*w_i/sum(w)+0.65*w_i*h(x_i)/sum(w*h), order by the persisted priority score h=P*G, draw independent stratified uniforms, assign post-resampling weight w_i/(M*q_i), transition under the stated P, and multiply by G.
auditor_independent_reimplementation.rng: numpy Generator PCG64, auditor seed 555000 for equal, 555001 for square-root, 555002 for reverse control
auditor_independent_reimplementation.interpretation: The main square-root result reproduces closely: 13.99% variance reduction in the independent implementation versus 14.13% in the worker certificate. The reverse-control degradation is directionally reproduced; the variance-ratio difference is about 1.74 approximate standard errors when accounting for the worker's 30k and auditor's 60k Monte Carlo sizes, so it is not a strong contradiction. All three independent means remain within one Monte Carlo standard error of the exact normalizing constant.

external_replication_search.result: No public hit for the worker-specific synthetic constants or allocation result. The public literature supports the mechanism class, not this exact internal synthetic experiment.

reproducibility_gaps: The worker certificate preserves model parameters, formulas, schedules and aggregate outputs but not the worker simulation source code, RNG seed/state, raw 30,000 replicate outputs or the 6,000-run pilot finite-difference raw samples.
The finite-model pilot A_t values are engineering estimates from repeated runs; they are not the single-run genealogy estimator advocated for production use.

The independent auditor implementation reconstructs the algorithm from the persisted contract and therefore validates reproducibility from specification, but it is not a bitwise/exact historical replay.
No protocol-matched external third-party reproduction was found.

supported: The exact two-state normalizing constants and square-root schedule are mechanically reconstructible from the persisted model and pilot A_t values.

On an independently reimplemented ordered-stratified simulator matching the persisted model contract, the square-root schedule again reduces fixed-budget variance by about 14% while preserving the normalizing-constant mean within Monte Carlo error.
The public SMC literature independently supports ordered stratification and generation-wise variance-based particle allocation as mechanism classes.
not_supported: A theorem that the 14.1% gain holds outside this finite synthetic model.
A claim that repeated-run pilot A_t estimation is production-ready or single-run online.
A claim that systematic resampling is generally inferior or invalid.
Any direct AGI, real-agent, human-label or tool-environment performance gain.
